system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: This asynchronous execution nature results in the conditional prompt mechanism used by Fast Mind as depicted in Fig. 8.
system_prompt_style.note: Fast Mind prompt sections switch between raw command, inferred intention and chat message depending on Slow Mind state; Chat & Assessment omits intention when no command.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The LLM takes as input the inferred intention, current orders, environment state, and action history.
env_context_strategy.note: Closest value: environment state (game state) is injected into the prompt; no repository or navigation tools. Game-domain mismatch.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: we use a compact representation for the action history by expressing consecutive repeated actions in the form of “action× repetition times” to reduce the length of the action history.
context_compaction.note: Closest value; heuristic compression of action history. FMOA baseline uses a max action-history length.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Current orders: Alice Soup (plenty of time), ...

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Each potential macro action candidate fills in the <next action> variable to evaluate its output probability.
tool_call_format.note: Mismatch: actions chosen by scoring LLM log-probabilities over 21 macro-action candidates, not parsing; no fitting value.

tool_count.evidence_quote: consequently resulting in a total set of 21 macro actions.
tool_count.note: Macro actions treated as action set; not function schemas.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: The established macro action set includes the following types.
edit_primitive.note: Game agent; macro action set contains no file editing.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Executor employs a script policy to convert macro actions generated by Fast Mind into atomic actions

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Chat & Assessment Stage runs periodically to actively monitor the command completion progress
loop_primitives.note: Hierarchical Slow Mind/Fast Mind/Executor pipeline running asynchronously.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: HLA adopts a hierarchical framework and comprises three modules

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: a proficient LLM, referred to as Slow Mind, for intention reasoning and language interaction, a lightweight LLM, referred to as Fast Mind, for generating macro actions, and a reactive policy, referred to as Executor

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Slow Mind sends the inferred human intention to Fast Mind and indicates to Fast Mind whether the command is successfully completed.
delegation_mechanism.note: Closest value; asynchronous intention passing between modules.

human_in_loop.note: Human is a co-player issuing commands, not a gating approver.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: The inferred intention is then stored by Slow Mind and sent to Fast Mind.

self_verification.evidence_quote: The completion assessment is used as a tool to keep track of command completion progress.
self_verification.note: Slow Mind (different model from Fast Mind) assesses completion; could be llm_judge.

termination_condition.note: Game ends on time budget; agent termination not described.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: a powerful LLM as used in Slow Mind is not applicable in Fast Mind due to huge inference latency. Therefore a lightweight LLM is more suitable.
cost_controls.note: Fixed role-based model split for latency, not dynamic routing.

guardrails.evidence_quote: We therefore employ an action filter to filter out sub-optimal macro actions.

target_domain.evidence_quote: we consider Overcooked as our testbed where players could communicate with natural language and cooperate to serve orders.

open_source.note: No repo URL in evidence; website only.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: We use GPT-3.5 [40] here as GPT-3.5 features strong reasoning and communication power.
model_agnostic.note: Uses GPT-3.5 and quantized Llama2-13B-chat (multiple vendors); no abstraction described.

first_release_date.note: Only v2 date (2024-01-09) visible; v1 date not in evidence.
